pe.name: Presentation Engine (rt-xr-unity-player with its glTFast loader)

cases.case: Media referenced by a circular buffer
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The player resolves each media entry to the circular buffers whose media index points at it and builds the pipeline from them; the texture and spatial-audio paths consume these buffers.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The Presentation Engine does not select an alternative: it hands every alternative of the media entry to the MAF, which opens the first one it can open.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Video buffer frames are presented against the audio clock when an audio reader exists, otherwise against an accumulated player time.

reading only; nothing was run. Every reference scene that uses it declares MPEG_media in the root extensions object, and the exporter emits it as a root-level child-of-root extension and marks it required.

cases.case: startTimeOffset is a number in seconds
cases.what: reading only; nothing was run. The only scene that sets startTimeOffset gives a number (0, the start of the source); the exporter never writes it, and the media access side performs the generation.

The exporter model can serialise endTimeOffset but the exporter never sets it (media are built with autoplay and loop only); the only scene that declares it gives endTimeOffset 0 with startTimeOffset 0 and loop true, which by the sentence ends generation at the start of the source instead of the end of the medium.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The rate is read from the accessor and passed to the buffer handler, which stores it as an interval that nothing uses; the player instead reads the buffer on every Unity Update.

The player requires the extension on media-backed accessors only to warn when missing (then null-dereferences in GetSuggestedUpdateRate), reads suggestedUpdateRate into MediaBufferHandler where updateRate is assigned and never used, and registers the header bufferView that nothing consumes; the extension does not drive timed access.

cases.case: Sample format extracted from the accessor and passed to the MAF
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Component type, sample type, byte offset, stride and attribute type of each media accessor are converted to the MAF buffer description.

cases.case: Header configuration from MPEG_accessor_timed passed to the MAF
cases.what: No header configuration from MPEG_accessor_timed reaches the MAF: BufferInfo passed to the pipeline has only bufferId, handler, componentType, type, offset, stride and attributeType; the player itself assumes immutable headers (CreateAccessorsHeaders(..., true)) and the video path only warns on immutable false or a header bufferView.

cases.case: Header presence taken from the bufferView attribute
cases.what: bufferView >= 0 only copies the view into the config map; header handling is not switched by it: MafAudioReader hard-codes useAccessorHeaders = true and the video texture path just warns when bufferView is present.

cases.case: Overwrite accessor and bufferView info from the header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The player does not overwrite accessor or buffer view values from a per-frame header: audio reads only the sample count and skips a fixed header length, and a video texture accessor with a header bufferView is only warned about.

cases.case: Audio delivered in the requested format
cases.what: Output format and channel count come from BufferInfo, but ENABLE_AUDIO_RESAMPLING is 0 so any mismatch of format, channel count or planarity throws 'buffer format doesn't match libav's decoder output format' instead of converting; only an exact match is delivered.

cases.case: Video delivered in the requested format
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The video decoder always converts to packed 24-bit RGB; the requested component type, sample type and plane layout in the buffer description are not read (a source comment marks this as to be done).

cases.case: Audio frames carry the timed accessor information header before the data
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. For audio the MAF writes a header per channel accessor at the start of each buffer frame and the samples follow it; it does so for every audio buffer, without regard to whether the scene signals a header.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The video decoder writes only pixel data into the buffer frame and never writes a header.

cases.case: Two bufferViews on a timed accessor
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Reference scenes give audio timed accessors both an accessor bufferView and a bufferView inside the extension, and the exporter writes both when headers are enabled.

cases.case: Accessor bufferView references the timed media data
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The accessor-level bufferView points at the 'MPEG_media.frame' view inside the circular buffer that receives the media.

cases.case: Extension bufferView points to the header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Where the extension has a bufferView it refers to a view named for the timed accessor header, 32 bytes for a scalar float accessor, in the same buffer; the exporter sets that view's length from the header field layout but never sets its offset (a misspelled attribute), so with several headers in one buffer the views would not be placed apart.

cases.case: No extension bufferView means no header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Video texture accessors omit the extension bufferView and no header view is reserved for them in the buffer; the exporter only adds a header view when headers are requested, which the video exporter does not do.

cases.case: Both bufferViews in the same buffer
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. In every reference scene with both views present they refer to the same buffer (checked for all scenes using the extension); the exporter builds the header view from the accessor view's buffer.

cases.case: Timed accessors point only to circular buffers
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Every timed accessor in the reference scenes refers through its bufferView to a buffer carrying the circular-buffer extension; the exporter creates the media buffer with that extension.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The extension appears only inside accessor objects in the scenes, and the exporter attaches it to accessors.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No reference scene sets immutable to false and the exporter never writes the flag, so a timed accessor whose type or component changes is not exercised.

cases.case: Extension bufferView buffer equals accessor buffer
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The header view and the accessor view name the same buffer in all scenes; the exporter copies the buffer from the accessor's view.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Accessors without an extension bufferView have no header view declared and none is reserved in the buffer layout, so the file is consistent with the assumption.

cases.case: immutable present and true when no header
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Timed accessors without an extension bufferView do not carry an immutable flag in any reference scene (the exporter never writes one), so the flag is not present as the sentence requires.
Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No scene or exporter code declares a header that changes (immutable false); only static-header configurations appear.

cases.case: Frames of the buffer may differ in length
cases.what: The player reads each frame with its own length (not the allocated size), and the buffer handler records the length of every frame written, so frames of different lengths are served.

cases.case: access by frame index or timestamp
cases.what: reading only; nothing was run. The player reads frames from the buffer by timestamp or by presentation time through the buffer handler's timestamped read, and falls back to sequential reads.

noted: The circular buffer itself is in the native MAF (BufferHandler::writeFrame stores frame->length per slot, ); slots are allocated at the buffer byteLength as maximum frame size (MediaPlayer.cs:298).

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. No circular buffer in any reference scene has a uri, and the exporter builds the buffer with uri unset.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The exporter sets the buffer length to the header sizes plus one frame's worth of accessor data, not multiplied by a frame count, and scenes that omit count (default 2) carry a length equal to a single padded frame (230400 x 4 bytes = 921600).

The scene-level attribute is not parsed and no deterministic or high-precision physics mode is enabled.
The scene-level attribute is not parsed; the physics rate is not set from the scene.

The scene trigger reports a collision only when every collision detector of the trigger currently collides (AND), not when any one does; and in the primitives form no targets are registered, so no collision is ever detected.

ProximitySceneTrigger.Init calls GetFirstActivatedCamera unconditionally, overwriting the configured referenceNode with the last camera in Camera.allCameras, so distances are measured to the camera whenever one exists.
When a node also carries a node-level proximity trigger the effective limits are initialised to zero and scaled by the weights, so the node is only close at distance zero.

The visibility trigger renders against the referenced camera on every evaluation with no check that the camera is active or enabled.
The trigger conditions are met only if every listed node is evaluated as visible by the camera.
The boundary property is parsed but never applied to capsule radius, top or base.
A cuboid primitive takes width on x, height on y and length on z.
A plane primitive is built in the x/z plane: its height is used as the z extent, not on y+.
The cylinder length runs along y, not z+.
Only the translation and rotation of the matrix are applied to a collision primitive; its scale is replaced by one.
The activate action inverts the status: ENABLED sets the target nodes inactive and DISABLED sets them active.
The combination string is reduced to its operator characters and applied pairwise left to right for & | ^ !; the negation sign ~ and parentheses are not understood.

ProcessState returns one activation value per frame and the later assignments override the earlier ones: EACH_ENTER and EACH_EXIT are returned on the transition frames as required, but ON is replaced by EACH_ENTER on the entry frame (and by FIRST_ENTER on the following frame the first time), and OFF by EACH_EXIT on the exit frame, so a behavior with ON or OFF is not launched on every frame the conditions are (not) met.
The first-enter control fires only on the second consecutive frame of the combination being met, because the entry frame is classified as each-enter.
The first-exit control never fires: the exit frame is always classified as each-exit, so the first-exit state is never reached.

Activation is computed by Behavior.ProcessState as one value per frame, so ON is reported only after the entry frames (the first frame yields EACH_ENTER, the second FIRST_ENTER) and an ON behavior does not fire while the conditions are being met on those frames; OFF, EACH_ENTER and EACH_EXIT match.
First-enter and first-exit are always overridden by the each-enter and each-exit results in the same evaluation, so behaviors configured with them never launch.

requirements.name: Media access function and buffer API / Media access function API

cases.what: Play() calls startFetching on the pipeline with a TimeInfo and ViewInfo. Rests on reading only.
Stop() stops the audio readers and calls stopFetching on the pipeline. Rests on reading only.

MediaPlayer.Dispose calls Stop, pipeline.Dispose and disposes the player's buffers, but the committed SWIG binding wraps the pipeline from createMediaPipeline with cMemoryOwn=false, so IMediaPipeline.Dispose only clears the handle and never calls delete_IMediaPipeline; the native pipeline is not destroyed and its resources are not freed by this path.
The binding defines IDLE, READY, ACTIVE and ERROR and the player acts on ACTIVE (presenting frames) and ERROR (flagging the failure). Rests on reading only.

cases.case: no tracks means all components accessed

The player passes a default ViewInfo only at startFetching and never supplies pose or object transform, so no distance-based detail is requested. Rests on reading only.
The player never fills ViewInfo.camera; it passes an empty ViewInfo. Rests on reading only.

Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The buffer handler has no releaseFrame method; a sequential read advances the read position and frees the slot implicitly.

cases.case: read_idx equal to write_idx means no frame
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. Availability is decided from a frame counter, and equal read and write indices with a non-zero count mean the buffer is full, not empty; the read index is the slot last read.

cases.case: No header in frame data when the Buffer API is used
cases.what: Frame index, timestamp and length are carried as fields of the Frame object passed to BufferHandler::writeFrame2, not serialised into the data; video frame data is raw pixels and audio frame data begins only with the Table 8 timed accessor information header (timestampDelta, byteOffset, count, ...), which Table 25 itself counts as part of the frame data, so no Table 25 buffer frame header is written into frame data.

cases.case: Header in frame data when the Buffer API is not used
cases.what: Rests on reading only; nothing was run. The MAF delivers frames through its own buffer handler, so the condition (an implementation without the Buffer API) is not met.
